title: Newsom Signs Bills Meant to Prevent Trump’s Interference in Midterms
summary: Gov. Gavin Newsom of California signed legislation that would make it illegal to interfere with ballots or election records in response to efforts by the president to restrict voting.

Gov. Gavin Newsom signed legislation on Saturday that is meant to prevent interference in California’s midterm elections in response to efforts by President Trump and other Republicans to restrict voting participation.


Mr. Newsom and fellow Democrats in the State Legislature crafted the bills to broadly combat involvement by the Trump administration, without knowing specifically whether or how the federal government might engage in California’s elections. The state relies heavily on mail ballots, and Mr. Trump has taken particular aim at that form of voting.


One[bill](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billNavClient.xhtml?bill_id=202520260AB282) prohibits the seizure of ballots, election records or voting technology before an election is certified.[Another](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202520260SB259) makes it a felony for people in positions of authority to direct their workers to interfere with the delivery of a mail ballot or its return to election officials.


Mr. Newsom signed a package of 13 bills, including a[measure](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billTextClient.xhtml?bill_id=202520260SB884) that prohibits arrests within 200 feet of a polling place on Election Day, with exceptions for acts related to disrupting the election or crimes against people or property. Democrats have feared that the Trump administration could send federal agents to polling places in immigrant communities.


Mr. Trump, who has[voted by mail twice](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/17/us/politics/trump-mail-vote-florida-election.html) this year, has claimed that absentee voting is rife with fraud. He and his administration[said in July](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/16/us/politics/trump-again-makes-unfounded-claims-of-noncitizen-voting.html) , without evidence, that California and three other states had allowed about 278,000 noncitizens to vote in federal elections.


California’s Democratic leaders said they were responding to a spate of unusual challenges from Mr. Trump, and local officials aligned with him. Mr. Newsom signed the bills in Los Angeles at the Japanese American National Museum, where Border Patrol agents[showed up](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/14/us/newsom-la-immigration-agents.html) outside a rally the governor held last summer.
